regulatory_history.notes: Settled allegations that Musical.ly collected personal information from children under 13 without parental consent.

procedural_note.text: The 2019 order permanently bars the companies from breaking the US children's privacy rule. On 2026-09-21 the court refused, for now, the government's request to lift it. As of 2026-10-06 no renewed motion to lift the 2019 order had been reported.

regulatory_history.amount: $300 million (+$100 million if the 2019 order is lifted)
regulatory_history.notes: Brought by the Justice Department with the FTC. Settled; the Justice Department said there was no determination of liability.

procedural_note.text: The court dismissed the case with prejudice on 2026-08-24, after the settlement. $100 million of the settlement is due only once the 2019 Musical.ly order is lifted. On 2026-09-21, in that older case, the court refused for now to lift it. As of 2026-10-06 no renewed motion to lift the 2019 order had been reported.

regulatory_history.title: Irish DPC fine over transfers of EEA users' data to China
regulatory_history.notes: Against TikTok Technology Limited, under GDPR Article 46(1) and transparency rules.

procedural_note.text: TikTok appealed. In June 2026 Ireland's High Court upheld the finding that TikTok broke EU privacy rules and told the regulator to reconsider its order to suspend transfers to China. On 2026-06-30 it proposed asking the EU Court of Justice about how the fine was calculated, so the appeal on the amount is still open.
